You add two DNS records: api.{{fqdn}} →: You add two DNS records: api.{{fqdn}} → {{api}} and *.apps.{{fqdn}} → {{ingress}}. Everything works natively with the cluster's own certificates: console, login, API and all applications.

It is shut down and kept as the template: It is shut down and kept as the template for Express clones (Masters tab). Clone it from the quick cluster card on the Install tab. It cannot be deleted while it has clones.
A master is an installed cluster kept as: A master is an installed cluster kept as a template: it is shut down and its disks are snapshotted. Clones are created from it in a few minutes instead of a full install, each with its own name, external addresses, host routes and credentials.
A clone is usable within minutes. It is: A clone is usable within minutes. It is fully isolated from its master and other clones (own admin certificates, service-account issuer and API CAs) when its Isolated condition turns True, about 15 minutes later.

Eligible: Ready clusters installed with: Eligible: Ready clusters installed with this tool, with the bastion load balancer and without nested storage or virtualization (support for those comes later). Clones are not eligible.
The cluster is shut down for good and it: The cluster is shut down for good and its disks are snapshotted. It stops being a usable cluster: it becomes the template for clones. Clones keep its internal name and current state, so prepare it (operators, content) before making it a master.
Refresh a master every few days: it boot: Refresh a master every few days: it boots, renews its certificates and takes new snapshots (about 20 minutes), so its clones start faster. Only possible while it has no clones.
Publish a route of the nested cluster un: Publish a route of the nested cluster under this cluster’s *.apps (its trusted certificate, no DNS): annotate it, and it appears here within about two minutes. Edge and reencrypt routes only; the hop from this cluster’s router to the nested cluster is plain HTTP.
